chunks: 94—What was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman or someone else, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“In every ghusl there is wudu, except ghusl for janabah.”

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If one performing ghusl from janabah finds moisture on the tip of his urethra or senses the خروج of something after his ghusl, then if he had performed istibra' in the manner we mentioned earlier, through urination or exertion, then no wudu is upon him, nor the repetition of ghusl, because that may perhaps have been wadhy or madhy, and purification is not invalidated by these two. But if he had not performed istibra' in the manner we explained, he repeats the ghusl. This is indicated by the following.

key_terms.اسْتَبْرَأَ: performed istibra', taking steps to ensure no residual fluid remains
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: state of major ritual impurity caused by janabah
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture or wetness found after purification
key_terms.مَذْيًا: madhy, a type of discharge mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.وَذْيًا: wadhy, a type of discharge mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does a person need wudu after ghusl of janabah, and what if moisture appears afterward?
ai.summary: This text discusses the legal ruling of wudu in relation to ghusl, stating an exception for ghusl of janabah. It also explains the ruling for moisture noticed after ghusl from janabah, distinguishing between one who performed istibra' beforehand and one who did not, with the latter being required to repeat the ghusl.
